findings.claim: In salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts, getClient bypasses refreshOAuthTokens, so the credential sync endpoint is never called in sync mode.
In zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts, refreshOAuthTokens is passed credentialId (credential.id) as its third argument, which is userId. The sync endpoint therefore receives the wrong calcomUserId.

minimumTokenResponseSchema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()]. These evaluate to literal, colliding property names instead of dynamic key matchers, so real token payloads fail validation or have every field except access_token stripped.
salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts uses prisma without importing it. It resolves only through globalThis.prisma, which is assigned only when NODE_ENV !== 'production'.

In salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts, getClient refreshes the OAuth token and saves it to the database. It then builds the jsforce.Connection from the stale credentialKey.access_token and instance_url instead of the refreshed values.
parseRefreshTokenResponse throws a generic error with no zod detail when parsing fails. The previous console.error of the failing response (e.g. in office365) was removed.

In sync mode, refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response; otherwise it returns refreshFunction()'s result. Callers in Google, HubSpot, Zoho CRM and Zoho Bigin expect an axios/gaxios/SDK shape (e.g. .data, expiresIn), so these reads are undefined or throw.
The webhook secret is compared with !== instead of a constant-time comparison.
parseRefreshTokenResponse sets a missing refresh_token to the literal string 'refresh_token'. Callers such as office365calendar and Zoom then persist it over the real stored refresh token.

googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts stores the entire parseRefreshTokenResponse safeParse wrapper ({success, data, ...}) as Credential.key instead of its .data. The next googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key) then throws.
The appSlug sent to the sync endpoint for Zoom is 'zoomvideo', but the app's slug is 'zoom', which the webhook uses to look up apps.
In sync mode, Zoom's expiry_date becomes NaN because fields are dropped, so zoomTokenSchema.parse fails.
In sync mode, Salesforce getClient parses the response with the stripping minimum schema, which drops instance_url and other fields.

In the credential webhook handler, appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body), symmetricDecrypt and JSON.parse run without error handling. Malformed bodies, bad ciphertext, a wrong key or invalid JSON therefore return 500 instead of 4xx.
The credential's invalid flag is never reset when the credential is updated.
The condition APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT is duplicated in refreshOAuthTokens.ts and parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts.
There is a redundant await/return wrapper at lines 13-19, and call sites use redundant async () => await wrappers.
getClient sends a refresh-token request every time the service is constructed, regardless of token expiry.
The webhook header lookup uses CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME as given. Node.js lowercases incoming header names, so a mixed-case configured name fails the lookup.
parseRefreshTokenResponse throws on parse failure and never returns success: false. The !success branches in Salesforce getClient and Zoom are therefore dead code.

The webhook looks up the credential with findFirst on userId+appId, but (userId, appId) has no uniqueness constraint. When a user has several credentials for the same app, an arbitrary one is updated.
The import '../oauth/decodeOAuthState' from inside the oauth/ directory should be './decodeOAuthState'.
APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is defined with && and so evaluates to string | undefined rather than a boolean.

parseRefreshTokenResponse switches to minimumTokenResponseSchema whenever credential sharing and the sync endpoint are configured, even when the refresh call still goes to the third-party provider (e.g. team credentials).
There is an empty /** */ doc comment.

The webhook looks up appStoreMetadata[app.slug], but appStoreMetadata is keyed by directory name rather than slug. Apps such as google-calendar, office365-calendar, msteams, zoom and lark-calendar therefore return 404 'App not found'.
The fetch call in refreshOAuthTokens has no error handling, so network failures throw unhandled exceptions.
The webhook's findFirst credential lookup ignores team credentials.
refreshOAuthTokens types refreshFunction as () => any and its response as any, which discards the return type and hides the fetch-vs-axios mismatch.
In sync mode, refreshOAuthTokens never checks response.ok or the response content of the fetch Response.
The credential-write webhook handler accepts any HTTP method instead of restricting to POST and returning 405.
Salesforce getClient checks response.statusText !== 'OK' instead of response.ok when handling the OAuth token refresh response.
There are no tests for the new credential-writing webhook or for the shared refresh/parse helpers.
The outbound POST to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT carries no secret or signature, so the receiver cannot authenticate the request before returning access tokens.
getClient hard-codes login.salesforce.com, which fails for Salesforce sandbox orgs.
The webhook header lookup does not handle array values. A header sent multiple times yields an array, and the string comparison against it lets the request through.
Office365 loses its expiry fields in sync mode, so a token refresh happens on every call.
office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts persists stale credentials when token parsing fails instead of throwing an error.
The webhook's read-then-write credential upsert can create duplicate credentials under concurrent requests because there is no unique constraint.
In zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts, appConfig.slug was replaced with the literal 'zoho-bigin', while appConfig.slug is still used on line 12.
The decrypted keys are written to credential.key without shape validation.
The external fetch in refreshOAuthTokens has no timeout.

coverage: pooled issues; severity and verdict are placeholders
